title: Understanding consumer decisions for more targeted adverts | World Economic Forum
gist: WPP Media and Oxford Saïd's 'How Humans Decide' study (1.2M+ purchase journeys, 47 countries) finds 84% of purchase decisions are effectively made before shopping starts due to 'priming bias', so advertising should build brand preference among out-of-market consumers. Reach is not influence: receptivity and touchpoint effectiveness vary sharply by category and journey stage, and owned/shared/earned channels can be ~3x more effective than paid media at conversion.

themes.theme: Priming bias: decisions made before shopping

insights.claim: WPP Media and Oxford Saïd Business School research analysing over 1.2 million purchase journeys across 47 countries and 200+ categories finds that 84% of consumer purchase decisions are effectively taken before people start shopping.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: Ad budgets concentrated on in-market, lower-funnel targeting may be mostly wasted; favours brand-building spend and media sellers offering upper-funnel reach.
insights.quote: 84% of consumer purchase decisions are effectively taken before people start shopping
insights.locator: The resulting report, How Humans Decide

insights.claim: Consumers normally considered 'not in the market' should be the principal audience for advertising, with messaging focused on building brand preference rather than simply capturing sales.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: Challenges performance-marketing orthodoxy; watch for budget shifts from search/retail media toward brand media.
insights.quote: most of the consumers normally considered as being not currently in the market for buying something should, in fact, be the principal audience for advertising
insights.locator: The resulting report, How Humans Decide

insights.claim: People are 10 times more likely to consider a brand they are biased towards and 14 times more likely to then buy it, so building 'priming bias' (familiarity, brand affinity, preliminary judgement) dramatically raises consideration and purchase odds.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: Brand equity is a measurable driver of conversion; companies with strong pre-existing brand affinity hold a structural sales advantage.
insights.quote: People are 10 times more likely to consider a brand they’re biased towards, and 14 times more likely to then buy it

insights.claim: The average shopper genuinely considers only two or three brands per product type, nearly always ones toward which they already have a positive predisposition, and this holds across every category studied from appliances to food.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: Winner-take-most dynamics in consideration: brands outside the 'top three' face steep acquisition costs; incumbents with mindshare are advantaged.
insights.locator: But when you ask people which

insights.claim: The narrow two-to-three brand consideration set appears to be an inherent human response to abundant choice rather than something marketing can easily alter, making long-run brand-building essential to rank in shoppers' 'top three'.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: Brand-building is groundwork that must precede purchase intent; short-term tactical spend cannot substitute.
insights.quote: this limitation is an inherent human response to the abundance of choice available to shoppers, and not something that marketing can easily alter
insights.locator: This behaviour appears across every product

insights.claim: Consumer receptivity to marketing varies widely: about 10% of consumers are likely influenced by almost any brand communication, while 23% are largely unreceptive to all forms of marketing.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: Treating audiences as equally influenceable embeds significant waste in marketing plans; targeting by receptivity is an efficiency lever.
insights.quote: While 10% are likely to be influenced by almost any form of brand communication, 23% are largely unreceptive to all forms of marketing

insights.claim: The single biggest determinant of a consumer's receptiveness to marketing is the product category: buyers of home appliances are about nine times more receptive than average, while toothpaste buyers are five times less influenceable.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: Considered-purchase categories get far more return on advertising than habitual staples; implies different marketing ROI profiles for durables vs FMCG firms.
insights.quote: people buying home appliances are typically nine times more receptive to marketing communication than the average person, while people buying toothpaste are five times less influenceable

insights.claim: Choosing four marketing touchpoints based on reach alone yields only about a 20% chance of affecting a purchase decision, while selecting the four most influential touchpoints raises that chance to 47%.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: Reach-based media buying (CPM-driven) underperforms influence-based selection by more than 2x; pressure on pure-reach media pricing models.
insights.quote: choosing four touchpoints based on reach alone creates only around a 20% chance of affecting a decision
insights.locator: Reach is not the same as influence

insights.claim: Because consumer receptiveness varies, ad exposure alone cannot be treated as evidence of influence, and businesses often mistake increased reach for increased marketing impact.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: Advertisers that keep optimising for reach will keep paying to persuade shoppers whose minds are already made up.
insights.quote: Until they accept that reach does not equate influence, advertisers will continue to spend money trying to persuade shoppers whose minds are already made up
insights.locator: More advertising or more effective advertising?

insights.claim: No combination of marketing touchpoints is equally effective across every category: a touchpoint that works for washing machine buyers may do little for shoe buyers, and tactics for milk or beer may be less effective for travel, telecommunications or banking.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: One-size-fits-all media plans are inefficient; agencies with category-level influence data have an edge.

insights.claim: Word of mouth has a 58% probability of influencing purchase in the personal care category but only a 2% probability for the average consumer in the supermarket category.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: Personal care brands benefit disproportionately from earned/social advocacy; grocery brands need other levers.
insights.quote: word of mouth is a particularly influential touchpoint, with a 58% probability of influencing purchase

themes.theme: Owned, shared and earned beat paid at conversion

insights.claim: Touchpoints most effective at brand building differ measurably from those most effective at converting sales, and owned (company website), shared (influencer content) and earned (word of mouth) channels can be nearly three times more effective than paid media at influencing the final purchase.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: Supports reallocation from paid media toward owned/earned and creator channels at the bottom of the funnel; a headwind narrative for paid-ad-dependent conversion.
insights.quote: can be nearly three times more effective than paid media at influencing consumers into the final purchase
insights.locator: Look beyond paid media to drive sales

insights.claim: Since 2020, the influence of social media influencers and creators on purchases has increased by 54%, and the influence of social media has risen by 143%, according to the How Humans Decide report.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: Structural tailwind for the creator economy and social platforms as purchase-influence channels.
insights.quote: Social media influencers and creators have increased in influence by 54% since 2020, for example, and social media has risen by 143%
insights.locator: And these touchpoints are only growing

insights.claim: Companies can target advertising more effectively by asking three questions: which consumers are open to being influenced, at what stage of the journey their preferences can be changed, and which touchpoints are most likely to influence their decision.
insights.speaker: SB
insights.so_what: A diagnostic for evaluating marketing efficiency of consumer-facing companies and ad-tech/agency offerings.
